creator: conflict-osint
topic: A $500 drone destroying a $4M vehicle is the most repeated statistic of this war, and the cost exchange it implies is not the one people think.
title: A notebook fact records how SURE you are, never how you KNOW — no provenance class exists
expected: Every fact carries a provenance class (e.g. directly-observed / claimed-by-an-interested-party / derived-from-documents / aggregator-restated) on an axis ORTHOGONAL to confidence, so a geolocated frame, a belligerent's press release and a budget-document inference can never be rendered at the same weight.
got: facts[] is {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?} where confidence is high|medium|low with a reason and source is one free-text string. No field records the KIND of knowing. The MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder the Gauntlet names is defined at knowledge/README.md:36-41 as the evidence contract for craft claims in PATTERNS.md about the corpus, requires transcript-style citation ('source · [mm:ss]' + the quoted line), and is never invoked by the schema or the prompt for research facts. A defence-ministry claim and a self-verified geolocation can both be honestly graded medium and are indistinguishable thereafter.
l2_priority: Attempt a real conflict notebook and record, per fact, whether provenance survived into the rendered script or was lost at the notebook boundary. Also confirm whether an executor spontaneously invents a provenance convention in `note` (which would make this a discoverability finding rather than a schema gap).
refuter_note: Challenged as (a) my topic being hard — refuted: the anti-pattern 'laundered confidence' at NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:107 shows the authors already recognise the failure in a market domain and gave it no mechanism; (b) present-but-missed — refuted: the ladder exists but governs a different artifact class and no notebook field references it; (c) lens — refuted: an added enum field and a prompt line would fix it inside the shared mechanism, so it defaults to content.

title: The only confidence-keyed rule fires on `low` — it guards against uncertainty and is silent on interest
expected: A second-source requirement that triggers on the SOURCE'S INCENTIVE as well as on uncertainty: a load-bearing fact sourced to a party with an interest in it needs corroboration regardless of how well-attested the statement is.

title: No naming policy anywhere in the conclusions layer, and the `unhinged` tier explicitly rewards motive claims about named people
expected: A naming rule in the conclusion contract: a conclusion that attributes motive or action to an identifiable person, unit or organisation is held to a source standard the falsifier does not supply, and is blocked outright at the `unhinged` tier. Falsifiability and safety are orthogonal — a falsifiable defamation is still defamation.
got: conclusions.ts contains no naming rule of any kind. LEAP_NOTE.unhinged advertises 'a claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended' as a feature, and `hottest` gives it UI prominence. The shipped worked reference does exactly this about a named living head of state and his donors, with a perfectly checkable falsifier attached. The same tier on a conflict topic produces a unit-level attribution from hours-old, single-sided footage, where being wrong is a real-world harm rather than a correction.
l2_priority: Produce the conclusion set for a live conflict topic and record every conclusion that names an identifiable actor, plus what the Creator's editor would say to each. This is the finding class the SKILL says only L2 produces.
refuter_note: Confirms BRIEF hypothesis 3 and states why the falsifier does not constrain it. Argued as `content` (a naming rule is a policy field, addable inside the shared mechanism); argued as `lens` because SKILL.md:196 already lists `conclusion-policy: max leap, falsifier standard, naming rules` as a lens field, implying the designers expect naming to be per-domain. Left `undecided` for the judge rather than claimed either way.

title: `verdict` is a mandatory confident one-sentence answer; there is no permitted shape for 'the evidence does not yet support a verdict'
expected: A verdict may honestly be conditional or withheld, and the quality bar scales with the unknown-to-fact ratio — a notebook where unknowns dominate is required to produce a conditional verdict rather than a declarative one.
got: `verdict` is 'the one-sentence answer', written during research 'because "answer early" means the script needs it at 0:40', and it is consumed by composition step 8. CRAFT-BASELINE §5 reinforces it: 'the answer comes early, not at the end.' Phase 2 provides an escape hatch for a missing TENSION ('if you cannot find one, stop and say so') and none for a missing verdict. Nothing in the quality bar scales with unknown count: a notebook with 30 unknowns and 10 facts satisfies it identically to one with three unknowns. For a topic that is hours old and contested, the schema structurally requires the confident synthesis the domain forbids.
l2_priority: Write a conflict notebook where unknowns outnumber facts and record whether the produced `verdict` is honest or whether the field's shape forced a claim. Then check whether the quality bar noticed.

title: Hedging is declared 'not a dial' and left unprotected — a measured 56% of epistemic marking was stripped from an already-approved chain
expected: Hedging density is word-budget exempt: a hedge may not be removed to meet a rate. The philosophy commitment 'tone may never change the beat chain' must extend to epistemic marking, because hedges are not beats and are therefore unprotected by it.
got: TONE.md §2 correctly identifies hedging as subject-determined and not a dial ('a creator who sets "confident" on an uncertain subject is asking the tool to lie') and §5 repeats it — then provides no protection. The Bitcoin run MEASURED a slow formal tone profile applied to an approved chain cutting hedges 7.8 → 3.9/1k, losing 5 of 9 hedges and 56% of the script's epistemic marking, with no dial set for either, because rate x duration is a word budget and hedges are the cheapest words in a script. The fix was drafted in that run as a proposed §2 protection row and never adopted into TONE.md. For a domain whose entire discipline is the distinction between 'we can see a vehicle burning' and 'the vehicle was destroyed', this silently converts a careful notebook into a confident script at render time.
l2_priority: Render a conflict script under two tone profiles and count hedges per 1k in both. Then check each surviving hedge against the fact's provenance — which, per G-2026-08-12-01, the script never received.
refuter_note: Challenged as my topic being hard — refuted: the effect was MEASURED on the incumbent market topic, not inferred from mine. Challenged as would-a-competent-execution-avoid-it — refuted: the measurement is OF the executed pipeline. Challenged as present-but-missed — the fix is present as a PROPOSAL in a run report, absent from the artifact, so it is present-broken and earns recurrence 2.

title: Columns absorb non-market material silently, and two `emptyMeans` mis-accuse a non-market notebook
expected: Column purposes describe the causal role the column plays, so a non-market topic can place material knowingly; `emptyMeans` states a defect the notebook can actually remedy in that domain.

Contradicts BRIEF hypothesis 1: the columns did not collapse and produced no underflow; the defect is silent absorption plus accusatory empty states.

title: No chain of custody for a primary artifact — a re-uploaded 2023 clip and a fresh geolocation are identical in the notebook

title: `tension.strength` conjoins three properties and has no honest value for 'widely held, checkable in principle, currently under-determined'
